description:
FILED s481b (2026-09-10, Opus) while measuring the critical-infrastructure
milestone (#1607).  It is the single reason `DBI.pm` cannot be loaded under
PCL, which closes the whole pure-Perl DBI route (DBI_PUREPERL=2 + DBD::DBM,
which works under real perl with no XS build at all).

REPRODUCER (scratch/s481b/probe-local-glob.pl), perl 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl:

    package Foo;
    our $DIR = "outer";
    sub show  { print "DIR=$Foo::DIR\n" }
    sub inner { local (*Foo::DIR, $@); $Foo::DIR = "inner"; show() }
    package main;
    Foo::show(); Foo::inner(); Foo::show();

    perl:  DIR=outer / DIR=inner / DIR=outer
    PCL :  read error during load: Package *Foo does not exist.
           Line: 56, Column: 16   <- the WHOLE file, nothing runs

THE EMISSION (from `pl2cl --module` on DBI.pm, line 1451):

    ;; local(*DBI::DIR, $@)
    (let ((*DBI::DIR (make-p-box nil))
          ($@ (make-p-box nil)))
      ...

`*DBI::DIR` is a bare CL symbol whose `::` makes the reader look for a package
called `*DBI`.  This is the #1570 failure MODE â an emitted file that cannot be
READ, so not one form in it runs and there is no drop, no refusal and no
diagnostic that names the construct.

THE UNQUALIFIED SPELLING IS FINE â measured, and that is the discriminator:

    our $X = 1;
    sub f { local *X; $X = 2; print "in=$X\n" }
    f(); print "out=$X\n";
    perl: in=2 / out=1      PCL: in=2 / out=1      (identical)

So the lowering of `local *GLOB` exists and works; it just does not run the
package-qualified NAME through the symbol speller (`Pl::CLForm::cl_sym` /
`cl_pkg`, the s423/#418 helper) the way every other qualified name is.

NOTE ON SCOPE.  `docs/not-supported.md` "local on hash/array elements and
typeglobs" covers `local *GLOB` semantics.  This task is NOT asking for those
semantics: it is asking that an unsupported (or partly supported) construct
never produce a file the READER rejects.  Even if the right answer is a ruled
refusal, it must be a refusal â loud, per statement, trappable â not the silent
loss of every other statement in the file.  Whichever way it goes, `DBI.pm`
needs the qualified spelling to load, because `local(*DBI::DIR, $@)` is inside
`DBI::_load_class`'s directory scan and DBI is unusable without it.

BAR: guard rows in a `Pl/t` file with both spellings and both packages, perl as
the oracle; the qualified form must either RUN like perl (preferred: it is one
speller call away) or refuse loudly with the rest of the file intact.
subject: `local *Pkg::NAME` (a PACKAGE-QUALIFIED typeglob) emits the bare CL symbol `*Pkg::NAME`, which the reader reads as package `*Pkg` â the WHOLE emitted file is unreadable ("Package *Foo does not exist").  The unqualified `local *NAME` works.  DBI.pm is lost to one such statement.
